They use their own buffers and check current protection for the owner each pulse; an absent player's wallet is never accessed. Unloaded chunks never run and time away never catches up. Paused or disabled systems retain contents. Collector transfer caps are **64 / 256 / 1,024 essence per second** total; condenser star draw caps **4,096 / 32,768**. No cables, remote networks or chunk loading are required.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.foundat: What this codex records, and how to begin

The Concordance is the practice of working with the Principles that run through the world. It begins with **looking closely**. Nothing in this codex teaches by being read: you learn by examining, studying and doing, and the codex records what you have learned.

Find something that holds its own light. Amethyst grows in geodes underground; glow lichen and glow berries hang in caves.\
\
**Sneak and use** a luminous specimen to examine it. Its glow is easiest to judge **in darkness**: a dark cave, or the open sky at night.
The Concordance has five stages: Initiate > Practitioner > Adept > Master > Architect. Each opens new practices; no one needs to follow every tradition.
The Concordance, its Principles and its resources

Every invocation spends **Focus**. You hold at most 20 points; one returns every 2 seconds, whatever you are doing. Focus is yours alone: no item, device or trade can store it.\
\
While you hold an instrument, your Focus shows at the bottom right of the screen.
An instrument channels invocations. Hold it in your **main hand**; the invocations you have understood appear on the spell bar, and the first is cast with the use key.

The spell bar lists your invocations in order. The **use key** casts the first; the number keys **2**, **3** and on cast the ones after it. While the instrument is in your hand those number keys cast instead of changing the hotbar slot: scroll to change slot, or bind Spell Engine's own spell keys in Controls to free them.
Everything you know and everything in your way, in one place

Press **J** (Controls: Concordance Journal) to open your journal. It shows what the server knows of your work: your Focus and stage, every research entry you have met and what its next state asks, each route to the next stage and what it still needs, and, once you know their traditions, your Vitae, the sky's forecast, your workers, deliveries, relics, the curses and wards on you, your Conclave standing, your spires and your Prima Materia.

Each line says in words where you stand and what to do next. **Exact values** (in the journal, or in the Concordance settings) add the figures behind them: how many of what each way needs, limits and caps. The same reports print in chat with **/jugcraft concordance status**, **stage**, **spire** and the other Concordance commands.

**Left**, **Right** or the section buttons change section; **Up**, **Down**, **Page Up** and **Page Down** scroll; **R** asks for the journal again; **X** shows or hides exact values; **Tab** moves between buttons; **Compose** opens the Spell Composer for the instrument in your hand; **Esc** closes it. With GuiLib installed the journal opens as a full workspace; without it, or with **Simple journal** chosen in the settings, it opens as a plain screen showing the same.
The ten Principles and the seven resources

- **Radiance**: light, revelation and sight\
- **Ember**: heat, combustion and change by fire\
- **Rime**: cold, stillness and preservation\
- **Tempest**: storm, charge and sudden motion\
- **Strata**: stone, structure and weight\
- **Verdance**: growth, life and renewal\
- **Tide**: flow, solution and exchange\
- **Tether**: binding, sympathy and agreements\
- **Echo**: memory, sound, dreams and knowledge\
- **Hollow**: absence, decay and endings

- **Focus** (personal attention)\
- **Ley Charge** (operational energy)\
- **Principle Essence** (material value)\
- **Vitae** (biological expenditure)\
- **Astral Resonance** (celestial alignment)\
- **Bound Will** (supernatural identity)\
- **Prima Materia** (equivalence value)\
\
Nothing turns one into another except a recipe that names both, with its loss.

Knowledge is not a resource. A research entry moves through four states, **Encountered**, **Observed**, **Understood** and **Mastered**, from evidence you gather yourself. Repeating the same observation adds nothing.
**Use** a blank sheet to write down every research entry you have begun, as far as you have come (up to understood). Anyone else can **use** your notes to read them; reading does not use them up.

Notes are a shared record, not experience. Where an entry accepts notes, reading them can stand in for one way of understanding it, but you must still encounter and observe it **yourself**, and mastery comes only from your own practice. Notes from the same writer count once, and your own notes teach you nothing new.
What the Concordance shows, and what it means

When something happens, the Concordance shows it where it happened, and only when it happened:
**Preparation**: glyphs drawn in, as a circle gathers.
**Execution**: light rising where work was done, or travelling along a real transfer: Ley Charge from a pylon to the circle it feeds, Radiance from a lantern into a pylon.
**Success**: a burst of light.

**Shortage**: grey smoke and sinking ash, with a hollow falling tone: something it needs is missing. A pylon short of charge, a missed upkeep, a formula without its ingredient, a worker that cannot go on.
**Danger**: flame and sparks thrown outwards, with a sharp rising warning: a circle's containment failing, a searing stir, a damaged spire.
Both sounds have subtitles.

A crucible's liquid stands at its real volume, in the colour of its strongest property, muddied when it is murky. A searing crucible smokes and spits. A spire shows whether it is being raised, working, lacking or damaged. A worker that lacks something waits, tapping or looking about; one held up on its way stands still. A finished circle glows until its result is taken.

The Concordance settings choose how much is drawn: **Full**, **Reduced** or **Minimal** (warnings only). Large workshops draw no more than a set amount each moment, and warnings are never hidden. **Reduced motion** keeps everything calmer.
Initiate, Practitioner, Adept, Master and Architect

The Concordance has five stages, each reached by any one of its routes once the stage before it is: they are the same stages as Jugcraft's (Discovery, Workshops, Specialization, Expeditions, Shared wonders). **/jugcraft concordance stage** shows yours and, for the next, every route and what it still needs.

Jugcraft's Discovery. Reached by any one of:\
- examine something that holds its own light

Jugcraft's Workshops. Reached by any one of:\
- understand First Light

Jugcraft's Specialization. Reached by any one of:\
- master two research entries\
- understand five entries in five traditions\
- understand Circle Lore and master First Light (the Adept's Attunement)

Jugcraft's Expeditions. Reached by any one of:\
- master five entries in three traditions\
- understand nine entries in seven traditions and master First Light\
- be a Luminary of the Starbound Conclave and master two entries

Jugcraft's Shared wonders. Reached by any one of:\
- be Starbound, help finish a Conclave project and master six entries\
- raise a Concord Spire, or help raise one
The Greenwardens' practice: habitats, cultivation and living devices
A producer, a consumer, a sensor and a collector

Set on a bed, it beats every 10 seconds: in its niche it spends 1 nutrient and makes 2 Verdance (1 while a factor is merely tolerable), up to 64. Beside a Ley Pylon it pours in, 3 Verdance for 2 Ley Charge. Its niche: moisture at least 2 (best 4+); light at least 8 (best 12+); nutrients at least 1 (best 4+); diversity at least 2 (best 3+); disturbance at most 10 (best up to 6).

Feed it plant matter (by hand or hopper): seeds, leaves and the crops are a quarter of a nutrient, chaff, vines and cane a half, fruit and roots three quarters, bread and hay a whole one. Every 2 seconds it eats one and, for every 4 quarters, gives a nutrient to the poorest bed within 3 blocks. Nothing composted gives back what it cost to grow.

Set on a bed, it reads the habitat there as a comparator signal: use it with an empty hand to choose a factor, or use a crop on it to read how well that crop would grow (15 thriving, 8 slowly, 0 not at all).
Harvests ripe crops within 3 blocks into its 9 slots (hoppers take them out), 1 Verdance a harvest, drawn from a Verdant Heart within 4 blocks.
Five factors, and where each comes from
The Greenwardens' crops grow only in a Verdant Bed, and only once a Greenwarden has woken it (an empty hand wakes it and up to 64 beds joined to it). It holds up to 32 nutrients.

**Moisture** (0 to 7): water within four blocks, rain, a wet sprinkler or a canteen keep a bed wet; every step of growth dries it by one.\
**Light** (0 to 15): sun or lamps at the plant, as the server's light has it; never the time of day.\
**Nutrients**: what the bed holds. Growth spends them.\
**Diversity**: the different plants in the 5x5 round it, itself included.\
**Disturbance**: working magic round it.

Nutrients come only from declared sources: **Mendvetch** (fixed from the air), the **Mulch Maw** (waste, at a loss), **bone meal** (2 a dose, on a bed or a crop in it) and **fertilizer**. A broken bed loses what it held.\
\
Disturbance: circle anchor 3, ley pylon 2, crucible 2, verdant heart 2, lumen sconce, lumen mote 1, warding stone 1, amethyst cluster, budding amethyst 1.

A crop grows on random ticks (and a sprinkler's) at full pace while every factor is ideal, at half pace while some are only tolerable, and not at all while one is outside its range. Look at it (or use it with an empty hand) to see which.

- **Sunpetal**: moisture at least 2 (best 4+); light at least 11 (best 13+); nutrients at least 1 (best 3+); diversity at least 1 (best 3+); disturbance at most 5 (best up to 2). It costs 1 nutrient a step; harvested, 2 and 1 chaff.\
- **Dewmoss**: moisture at least 5 (best 7+); light at most 12 (best up to 9); nutrients at least 1 (best 2+). It costs 1 nutrient a step; harvested, 2 and 1 chaff.\
- **Gloamcap**: moisture at least 2 (best 3+); light at most 9 (best up to 6); nutrients at least 2 (best 4+); disturbance at least 1 (best 3+), at most 15 (best up to 10). It costs 2 nutrients a step; harvested, 1 and 1 chaff.\
- **Mendvetch**: moisture at least 1 (best 3+); light at least 8 (best 11+); disturbance at most 6 (best up to 3). It gives 1 a step; harvested, 1 and 1 chaff.

A ripe crop (step 3) is harvested with an empty hand, or by a Gleaner: its produce and Verdant Chaff, and it falls back to step 1 to grow again. A Mendvetch next to other crops also speeds them, as legumes do.
Your first Sunpetal comes from the crafting grid; after that, its harvests give more.
Your first Dewmoss comes from the crafting grid; after that, its harvests give more.
Your first Gloamcap comes from the crafting grid; after that, its harvests give more.
Your first Mendvetch comes from the crafting grid; after that, its harvests give more.

Once you understand First Light, look closely at living things. **Sneak and use** one of these to examine it:\
- Moss Block\
- Sunflower\
- Brown Mushroom\
- Lily Pad\
- Fern
Study one at a **Lampwright's Bench**, or read someone's **Research Notes**.
Your touch now wakes Verdant Beds and living devices. To **master** Verdant Husbandry, harvest each of the four crops by hand.
You know a garden as well as it knows itself.
The Hearthbinders' practice: fire kept and used

Once you understand First Light, look at fire as the Hearthbinders do: something kept and used, never let loose. **Sneak and use** one of these to examine it:\
- Coal\
- Charcoal\
- Torch\
- Campfire\
- Magma Block\
- Blaze Powder\
- Blaze Rod\
- Magma Cream\
- Fire Charge
You have examined 3 different things that hold fire. Study one at a **Lampwright's Bench**, or read someone's **Research Notes**.

You can now cast **Hearthspark**, **Hearthguard** and **Cinderbolt** with any Concordance instrument. To **master** Hearthbinding, kindle 3 different kinds of hearth with Hearthspark: a campfire, a soul campfire, a candle, a candle cake.
You can now cast **Hearthflare**, and your Ember invocations cost a point less Focus.

The Hearthbinders' gear gives **fire Spell Power**. Cinderbolt and Hearthflare add half a point of damage for each whole point of it: two points make one more. Wear a **focus** in the Spell Focus slot and a fire set as armour; the most is +6, so Cinderbolt deals 6 and Hearthflare 7. The **Fire Bangle** goes in a Bracelet slot. None of it holds Focus: Focus is yours alone.
+2 fire Spell Power while worn in the Spell Focus slot. One focus at a time.
Pyromancer's set: 7 protection for the whole set.
Pyromancer's set: 7 protection for the whole set.
Pyromancer's set: 7 protection for the whole set.
The lesser focus set with diamonds: +4 fire Spell Power in the Spell Focus slot.
Once you understand Hearthbinding, your melee blows leave the creature smouldering for 3 seconds, wherever you may harm it. It gives no Spell Power, and a second bangle adds nothing.

Each piece of either set gives half a point of fire Spell Power, so only four pieces together raise fire damage, by one. The **Pyromaniac's** set is cloth: a little less protection than leather. The **Pyromancer's** set, wool and gold, has leather's protection and lasts longer. Spell Power's own enchantments cannot be put on either.
Pyromaniac's set: 5 protection for the whole set.
Pyromaniac's set: 5 protection for the whole set.
Pyromaniac's set: 5 protection for the whole set.
Pyromaniac's set: 5 protection for the whole set.
Pyromancer's set: 7 protection for the whole set.
Fire that stays with its target

A smouldering creature burns as anything on fire does, a point of damage a second, while the status lasts. Water and rain put it out; Fire Resistance and creatures born of fire ignore it; milk cures it. It never sets blocks alight.
Hearthspark lights a hearth as flint and steel would, and only where you could light it by hand: claims, protected towns and spawn protection refuse it. It never places fire.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.hexes.d: Sympathy and its remedies, and dreams that give back all you had
Dreams, and waking with all you had

Once you understand First Light, examine something from the edge of dreams (**sneak and use**): chorus fruit, an ender pearl, a white bed, a spore blossom. Study one at a Lampwright's Bench to understand Dreamwalking.

Use the censer at night (10 Focus) to dream. Everything you carry is held for you; you dream in adventure mode, with nothing, for at most 180 s, within 24 blocks of your body. Catch the dream wisps by walking into them: 3 gather at once and one more every 30 s; each is one dreamglass, at most 8. Use the censer again to wake.

However a dream ends, you wake with exactly what you carried, in the same slots, where your body lay, and never with more experience than you had (experience gained in the dream is gone; experience spent there, on an enchantment or a repair, stays spent). Anything you picked up while dreaming falls at your feet. You keep the dreamglass you caught; half if you strayed (left the dimension or went too far) or were hurt; none if you died (then your body dies with what it carried). Leaving the server mid-dream wakes you; a dream left open by a crash ends when you next join. Nothing worn in an accessory slot may come into a dream.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.hexes.s: Links, curses, investigation, remedies and wards

Once you understand First Light, examine a likeness (**sneak and use**): a fermented spider eye, a cobweb, a poisonous potato, a rabbit's foot, an armor stand. Study one at a Lampwright's Bench to understand Sympathy.

Use a taglock on a creature to take a **link** to it. A fresh link has strength 100 and loses one every 12 s: it fades in twenty minutes. No link can be taken to yourself, to a player the server's rules do not let you harm (PvP off, or your party), or to anyone warded against linking. Every use checks the link again: its target must be in your dimension, within 128 blocks, and still yours to act against.

Hold a linked taglock with a curse's reagent in your other hand and use it. A curse is bounded: a hindrance, never harm, for minutes, never forever. Each pulse is checked again: it skips while you are elsewhere or out of range or they are warded, and lifts for good if the rules stop letting you harm them.\
- **Curse of Lethargy**: cobweb casts it; slowness for 10 s every 20 s, for 300 s in all; needs link strength 30 and 6 Focus; lifted by sugar\
- **Curse of Misfortune**: rabbit foot casts it; unluck for 30 s every 30 s, for 600 s in all; needs link strength 20 and 4 Focus; lifted by amethyst shard\
- **Curse of Frailty**: fermented spider eye casts it; weakness for 10 s every 20 s, for 300 s in all; needs link strength 40 and 8 Focus; lifted by blaze powder

Something weighs on you? Use a **scrying glass** (2 Focus a look). The first look names each curse and its remedy; the second names who cast it, unless they are warded against scrying. Hold the remedy in your other hand and use the glass to lift the curse (the remedy is spent). With a taglock in your other hand the glass reads its link. **/jugcraft concordance hexes** lists what you know. Anyone may use a scrying glass.

A ward sigil wards you against one kind of operation for twenty minutes (a fresh one renews it; wards never stack). Anyone may make and use one.\
- **Linking**: no taglock can take a link to you (paper, dreamglass and string)\
- **Cursing**: no curse pulse reaches you (paper, dreamglass and amethyst shard)\
- **Scrying**: no scrying glass can name you as a caster, nor show where you are (paper, dreamglass and ink sac)\
- **Moving**: no one else's Concordance effect can push you (paper, dreamglass and iron ingot)
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.invocat: Defense: Wraps you in a shell of dawn light that absorbs the next blows.

Wraps you in a shell of dawn light that absorbs the next blows.\
\
**Defense.** Absorbs up to 8 damage for 10 seconds.\
\
5 Focus (4 once First Light is mastered), cast 0.4 seconds, cooldown 12 seconds. Learned when First Light is understood.

Tunings:\
- **Prolong**: absorbs up to 8 damage for 20 seconds (+1 Focus)\
- **Intensify**: absorbs up to 12 damage for 10 seconds (+2 Focus)\
\
**Counter.** A burst of damage breaks the shell, it fades after 10 seconds, and the cooldown leaves two seconds bare; it does not stack with itself.
Damage: A burning shard: fire damage to the first creature it meets, which then smoulders. Stronger with fire Spell Power.

A burning shard: fire damage to the first creature it meets, which then smoulders. Stronger with fire Spell Power.\
\
**Damage.** Reach 16 blocks. 3 fire damage (+0.5 per point of fire Spell Power); Smoulder for 3 seconds.\
\
5 Focus (4 once Hearthbinding is mastered), cast 0.5 seconds, cooldown 2 seconds. Learned when Hearthbinding is understood.

Tunings:\
- **Extend**: reach 24 blocks (+1 Focus)\
- **Intensify**: 4 fire damage (+0.5 per point of fire Spell Power); Smoulder for 3 seconds (+2 Focus)\
\
**Counter.** It needs a clear line and strikes one target; water, rain and Fire Resistance put out the smoulder, and fire-born creatures shrug it off.
Spells the traditions wrote down, and how to answer them
Movement: Carries you a few blocks the way you face, in a flash.

Carries you a few blocks the way you face, in a flash.\
\
**Movement.** A push of 1.2 blocks a tick.\
\
4 Focus (3 once First Light is mastered), instant, cooldown 4 seconds. Learned when First Light is mastered.

Tunings:\
- **Intensify**: a push of 1.8 blocks a tick (+2 Focus)\
\
**Counter.** Walls stop it, knockback resistance shortens it, and it cannot be used again for 4 seconds.
Damage: A burst of fire round you: fire damage to the nearest creatures, which then smoulder. Never you; stronger with fire Spell Power.

A burst of fire round you: fire damage to the nearest creatures, which then smoulder. Never you; stronger with fire Spell Power.\
\

An invocation is a spell someone wrote before you, in the same words you compose with and under the same limits. You learn it from research, not from an item: an instrument only lets you cast what you have learned. Each has one **role**: damage, defense, movement, support, investigation or utility.

An invocation can be **tuned** with one modifier from the short list it allows, if you could use that modifier yourself. Tuning changes its numbers, never what it does, and costs that modifier's Focus with every cast. Type `/jugcraft concordance tune` with an instrument in hand to see your tunings, `tune <invocation> <modifier>` to set one and `tune <invocation> clear` to remove it.

Glyphs are the building blocks that make up spells. A spell’s outcome is determined by which Glyphs are used and in what order they appear. They fall under three major categories: Forms, Effects, and Augments.
Form Glyphs are the vessels that deliver the contents of a spell to the target. Every spell must begin with a Form, and only one Form may be present. Effect Glyphs determine what a spell will do once it reaches its target. Spells can contain multiple Effects and will resolve in the order they are placed during spellcrafting.
Augment Glyphs change the properties of the Form or Effect Glyph to their left as long as they are compatible. Multiple Augments may be chained together to modify the same Glyph. Augments have no effect on other Augments. Glyphs fall into tiers of I, II, or III. The Novice’s Spell Book can only cast tier I Glyphs, but higher tiers will be available each time you upgrade your Spell Book.

A focus that modifies effects that move, create, or modify blocks. Blocks that you move with effects like Launch, Gravity, Pull, Knockback, etc. will now deal damage to entities they hit. Damage is increased by Spell Damage, block hardness, and the speed of the block. Additionally, effects that target or create blocks will duplicate the rest of the spell targeting the new block or moving block.

Modifying or creating a block will duplicate the rest of your spell onto that new block. For example, Freeze -> Break will freeze the block, and cast break onto that block. Without the focus, break would only be applied to the block that was hit originally. Effects that will duplicate this target include glyphs such as Conjure Mageblock, Freeze, Break, Exchange, Place Block, and more. Using AOE on these effects will duplicate the spell onto every block.

Effects that move blocks will duplicate the rest of the spell onto those moving blocks. To see this in action, try using Conjure Mageblock -> Launch -> Delay -> Knockback to send a block flying in the direction you are looking. This targeting system applies to all moved blocks. Using AOE on block moving effects will let you manipulate many blocks at once.

Throw Ice: Conjure Water -> Freeze -> Launch -> Delay -> Knockback. Damage and ignite hit targets: Conjure Mageblock -> Launch -> Ignite -> Delay -> Knockback. Ignite TNT: Place Block (TNT) -> Ignite. Throw Exploding Terrain: Launch -> Delay -> Knockback -> Delay -> Explosion. Throw many blocks: Launch -> AOE x2 -> Delay -> Knockback. Pull blocks: Pull -> AOE x2 -> Delay -> Duration Down -> Launch -> Delay -> Knockback. Harvest Sand: Crush (on stone) -> Aoe -> Break

Whirlisprigs are curious nature sprites that are exclusively found in forested areas. Summoned Whirlisprigs can be given a home in the world, and will begin producing natural materials including wood, crops, seeds, and flowers that exist around them. Wild Whirlisprigs can be befriended and will drop Whirlisprig Tokens if a tree is grown near them.
Whirlisprigs will follow animals, players, and monsters! They will also grow grass around them every once and a while.

To summon a Whirlisprig, use a Whirlisprig charm on any flower. Whirlisprigs consider their home to be 10 blocks in any direction from the flower. Whirlisprigs require source nearby to operate, and will only generate items if there is a chest placed next to the flower. You can get your charm back by using Dispel on a Whirlisprig. They may be given orange, yellow, white, or green dye.

Summoned Whirlisprigs must be happy in order to produce materials, and their mood is determined by the number and diversity of natural materials in their home. You may use blocks on the Whirlisprig to gain additional info if a Whirlisprig would enjoy that block in their home. Interacting with the Whirlisprig with an empty hand will give you additional info on the Whirlisprig's happiness.
Note: It can take several minutes for a Whirlisprig to update its mood after placing a block. Whirlisprigs value diversity, and too much of one block will no longer count.

Drop rates are determined by happiness, diversity, and the proportions of blocks in a Whirlisprig home. For example, to generate a lot of logs, grow more trees. To gain more seeds and crop harvests, plant more crops.

When using multiple Wixies, you may wish to lock a jar to a specific potion. Wixies will only output potion to jars that contain the same potion, or an unlocked empty potion. Each craft costs Source. See the section on the Potion Jar for more information.

book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.radianc:
Some things hold light of their own. **Sneak and use** one to examine it.\
\
Luminous specimens:\
- Amethyst Shard\
- Glowstone Dust\
- Glowcap\
- Glimmerbloom\
- Jack-o'-Lantern Mushroom\
- Glow Ink Sac\
- Glow Lichen\
- Glow Berries
You have handled a luminous specimen and noticed its glow. Now judge it where there is no other light.

In darkness (light 4 or less) the glow is the specimen's own. To **understand** it, study a specimen at a **Lampwright's Bench**, examine 3 different specimens in darkness, or read **Research Notes** from someone who has understood it.

Radiance can be gathered and set loose. You can now cast **Kindle**, **Dawn Aegis** and **Revelation** with an instrument, and kindle, infuse and channel lanterns at a Lampwright's Bench.\
\
To **master** First Light, Kindle light in 8 different chunks.
You can now cast **Lance of Dawn**, **Flashstep** and **Lanternward**, and every First Light invocation costs less Focus (see Invocations).

Use it to light it or put it out. Lit, it burns one Radiance every 20 seconds whether carried or not, and while it is in either hand the air round you is lit (light 12). Put out, it has spent the measure it was burning. It holds up to 64 Radiance.\
\
A lantern can be given or traded; anyone may carry its light, but only someone who understands First Light can recharge it.
The bench holds one specimen and one piece of work. Its buttons say what they need when they cannot run.

**Study** reads a specimen for 5 seconds. The specimen is held while it is read and used up only when the study finishes; cancel, break the bench or take the specimen and nothing is lost. If you are away when it finishes, the bench keeps your notes until you next open it.

Once First Light is understood: **Kindle** turns a lantern and an amethyst shard into a Kindled Lantern with 8 Radiance. **Infuse** adds a specimen's Radiance to a Kindled Lantern, up to 64; a specimen that would overfill it is refused. **Channel** spends 6 Focus for 2 Radiance.\
\
- Amethyst Shard: 8 Radiance\
- Glowstone Dust: 6 Radiance\
- Glowcap: 4 Radiance\
- Glimmerbloom: 3 Radiance\
- Jack-o'-Lantern Mushroom: 3 Radiance\
- Glow Ink Sac: 3 Radiance\
- Glow Lichen: 2 Radiance\
- Glow Berries: 1 Radiance
A brass stand that burns Radiance for a steady light 15: one measure every 60 seconds, up to 64 measures.

Use it with a **Kindled Lantern** to pour up to 16 Radiance in; what does not fit stays in the lantern. Anyone may pour, so a Lampwright can keep a town's lamps lit. **Sneak** to draw Radiance back into your lantern: only the sconce's owner may. Only Radiance burns in a sconce, and broken, it keeps what it held, less the measure it was burning.
Relics that work where they are meant to, and say why not elsewhere
Relics, where they work, and the Reliquary Shrine

Once you understand First Light, examine something that has outlived its maker (**sneak and use**):\
- Heart of the Sea\
- Nautilus Shell\
- Totem of Undying\
- Eye of Ender\
- Recovery Compass\
Study one at a Lampwright's Bench to understand Relic Lore.

A relic works only where it is meant to: **held** in a particular hand, **worn** in an armour slot or an accessory (Trinkets) slot, or **installed** in a Reliquary Shrine. Each relic names its places.\
Anywhere else it does nothing: carried loose in your inventory, worn for show in a cosmetic slot, held in the other hand, or kept in a chest, a shulker box or a bundle (nothing inside those is ever looked at).\
**/jugcraft concordance relics** lists the relics you carry, where each one is, and whether it works or exactly why not.

Holds 64 charge.\
- **held in the off hand**: glowing on hostile creatures within 12 blocks for 3 s, every 2 s, 1 charge a pulse\
- **installed in a Reliquary Shrine**: glowing on hostile creatures within 24 blocks for 3 s, every 2 s, 1 charge a pulse\
- anywhere else it does nothing, and says why

Holds 48 charge.\
- **worn in an accessory slot**: regeneration on you for 5 s, every 10 s, 2 charge a pulse; needs ten calm seconds, someone hurt\
- **installed in a Reliquary Shrine**: regeneration on your party within 8 blocks for 5 s, every 10 s, 1 charge a pulse; needs someone hurt\
- anywhere else it does nothing, and says why\
- binds to the first player it serves, and then serves only them

Holds 32 charge.\
- **held in the main hand**: speed on you for 3 s, every 2 s, 1 charge a pulse; needs the open sky above\
- cannot be installed\
- anywhere else it does nothing, and says why

Holds 32 charge.\
- **worn on the head**: night vision on you for 22 s, every 10 s, 1 charge a pulse; needs the dark of night\
- cannot be installed\
- anywhere else it does nothing, and says why

Use a relic on an empty shrine to **install** it, if it has an installed way of working. Use any other relic on it (or one that cannot be installed) to **recharge** it: each Ley Charge from the Ley Pylons within 2 blocks gives 4 charge. An installed relic is charged from those pylons as it works, 8 a second. Use the shrine with an empty hand to take its relic back. Only its owner and their party may use it.

However many relics you carry and wear, they pulse at most 2 times a second together; one owner's shrines, at most 4. A relic held back waits a second and is not spent. A relic spends charge only when its pulse changes something, and two relics giving the same effect never add up: the stronger holds.

Once you understand **Relic Lore**, you can wear these: a belt in the Belt slot, a charm in a Charm slot (a Leather Belt gives a second) and up to 2 on your feet. They hold no Focus or charge and need no pylon. Two of a kind never add up; a second vial only waits its turn. The Leather Belt and the Amphibian Boots show on you unless armour covers them, and the Concordance settings can hide them from everyone.
One more Charm slot. Take the second charm off before the belt.

A fall's harm comes from your food instead of your health, at 0.5 food a point (blows in quick succession are paid once), and you jump a little higher. A fall your food bar cannot pay for hurts as ever.
The same for fire and hot floors, not lava.
A blow that would kill you leaves you on 2 hearts, healing for 5 seconds, and the vial is used up. It does not answer a fall into the void, a held totem (the totem answers), or a death in a dream.

Three Angelheart Vials and an Angelic Feather, crafted together. A blow that would kill you leaves you at full health, healing and proof against fire for 10 seconds, and the down becomes an Angelic Feather where it was worn. Until then it is a feather as well. A vial worn beside it answers first.
Three Angelheart Vials and an Angelic Feather.
You swim faster, and your air lasts about twice as long.

A little knockback resistance. A fall that hurts you sends a wave through the ground: up to 12 hostile creatures within 3 blocks (more for a harder fall, at most 6) are harmed, thrown back and slowed. A few great foes, such as the Warden, take the harm but are neither thrown nor slowed.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.sky.att: The astrolabe and what it gives

It holds up to 32 resonance. Use it where you can see a risen pattern: it spends the pattern's cost and attunes you to it, and its effect is yours while the pattern stays up (at most 8 minutes; use it again to renew). Death ends an attunement.

A master may attune when nothing is up, by **recalling** the pattern they last observed: it costs the pattern's recall price and lasts 2 minutes, once each time the pattern comes round. Stored resonance is the alternative to waiting, never a way round the sky's count.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.sky.cal: The sky keeps the world's own clock, the one the sun and moon follow: a day is 20 minutes, night runs from 19:00 to 05:00, and the moon goes from full to new and back every 8 days. Every player sees the same sky, and so does the world after a restart. What your screen draws (a shader's moon, your render settings) never changes what is up.

- **The Full Moon**: on the full moon's night, 19:00 to 05:00, a clear sky. Pays 4 resonance; Moonsight: you see in the dark while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.\
- **The New Moon**: on the new moon's night, 19:00 to 05:00, any weather. Pays 4 resonance; Spring Tide: you breathe under water while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.\
- **The Lantern Star**: every 3 days (days that leave 1 over 3), 18:00 to 20:00, a clear sky. Pays 2 resonance; Lantern Hands: you dig and work faster while it is up. Attuning costs 2, recalling 6.\
- **The Echo Comet**: every 19 days (days that leave 7 over 19), 20:00 to 04:00, a clear sky. Pays 8 resonance; Comet's Wake: you run faster while it is up. Attuning costs 6, recalling 16.\
- **The Winter Crown**: every 2 days (days that leave 1 over 2), in winter, 21:00 to 03:00, a clear sky. Pays 3 resonance; Frostmantle: fire does not burn you while it is up. Attuning costs 3, recalling 9.\
- **The Harvest Moon**: every night, in the Harvest Moon, 19:00 to 05:00, any weather. Pays 6 resonance; Feast Favour: villagers trade with you as with a hero while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.

Use an Orrery Observatory with an empty hand, or ask with **/jugcraft concordance sky**, to read the forecast: today's day, time, moon and season, and every pattern up now or rising in the next 8 days, with when it rises, the weather it needs and the time of year it keeps to.

Some patterns keep to a time of year. The Winter Crown comes round only in Jugcraft's winter (the server's date; with seasons off, all year). The Harvest Moon pattern is the Halloween event's own Harvest Moon: it rises on the nights the event says, and never outside them.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.sky.cel:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at the instruments that measure the sky. **Sneak and use** one of these to examine it:\
- Spyglass\
- Clock\
- Compass\
- Phantom Membrane\
- Glow Ink Sac
Study one at a **Lampwright's Bench**, or read someone's **Research Notes**.

Your touch now aligns an Orrery Observatory, and an Astrolabe answers you. To **master** Celestial Attunement, observe 3 different patterns through an observatory (use it with an empty hand while one is up).
You can recall a pattern you have seen when the sky is empty.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.sky.des: The Starwatchers' practice: celestial patterns, observatories and attunement
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.sky.obs: Set it under the open sky in the Overworld. Placed by a Starwatcher it is aligned to them; otherwise a Starwatcher's empty hand aligns it. Every 5 seconds it looks up: from each pattern up and in view it gathers that pattern's resonance, up to 32.

Each time a pattern comes round it pays its keeper once, however many observatories they keep. Turning the world's clock back brings back only nights that have paid; turning it forward cannot pay sooner than half the pattern's period of real play. Its keeper's party may draw its resonance into an astrolabe (use the astrolabe on it).
It says why it is idle: nothing up, unaligned, clouded over (for a pattern that needs a clear sky), something hiding the sky, not in the Overworld, full, already gathered, or too soon.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.tooltip: A record of what you have learned of the Principles
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.vigil.c:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at living things that bleed or sting. **Sneak and use** one of these to examine it:\
- Sweet Berries\
- Crimson Roots\
- Crimson Fungus\
- Nether Wart\
- Spider Eye
Study one at a **Lampwright's Bench**, or read someone's **Research Notes**.
The Crimson Chalice answers you now. To **master** Crimson Rites, grow a Thornheart Blade you wield to its second stage.
You know what a life can give, and what it cannot.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.vigil.d: The Crimson Vigil's practice: offerings, Vitae and living equipment
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.vigil.o: Use it to make an **offering**: 4 health for up to 4 **Vitae**, which the chalice holds (up to 32). An offering never leaves you below 8 health, never comes within 5 seconds of the last, and takes no health when the chalice is full.

**Health** is yours to heal as ever. **Vitae** is what an offering made of it. **Exhaustion** is what offering leaves behind: each offering adds 3 points, and they clear one every 2 minutes and by nothing else: no food, potion, spell or regeneration. Healing to full does not let you offer again as if fresh.

An offering's yield falls with your exhaustion: 0 to 3 points: 100%; 4 to 7 points: 50%; 8 to 11 points: 25%; at 12 no offering at all. Rounded down. So a careful offering now and then gives far more than many in a row. **/jugcraft concordance vitae** says all three, and how long until you are clear.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.vigil.s: **Sneak and use** the chalice: 6 Vitae become 6 Focus at once, at most once a minute and never beyond your full Focus. An emergency measure: what you can offer in an hour is bounded by your exhaustion, so it never becomes a spring of Focus.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.vigil.t: A living sword. It grows by three kinds of deed: **slaying** hostile creatures, **enduring** harm while you wield it, and being **nourished** (use the chalice with the blade in your other hand: 2 Vitae for 8 vigor).

Each deed pays by how often its kind of creature or harm has come up today: 4, 2, 1, 1, then nothing; each kind of deed pays at most 24 a day. A mob farm or a cactus stops paying at once. Its stages need several kinds: Awakened (20, two kinds with 5), Grown (60, every kind with 10), Flourishing (150, every kind with 30).
Each stage adds 1 attack damage while the blade has vigor; every blow on a living creature spends 1. Without vigor its powers sleep, but nothing it has grown is lost.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.wonders: The Concordance's endgame wonder: founded, raised and kept

A Concord Spire is raised round a **Spire Heart** by a **Master** of the Concordance, and works only while it is kept: supplied every day, whole, and attended by keepers who go on practising its tradition. It is founded in one of three **configurations**, each with its own research, practice, crown, upkeep and field. A spire is the world's, not the heart's: breaking the heart, leaving or a restart loses nothing, and a heart put back where it stood answers again.

Place the heart where the spire will stand. **Sneak and use** it with an empty hand to choose a configuration (it says what each needs), then **use** it to found the spire. Afterwards an empty hand shows how it stands; its keeper sneaking shares it with their party or takes it back.

A spire is raised in four phases, in order:\
1. **Foundation**: four Ley Pylons and four Warding Stones round the heart, as a Lesser Circle has them.\
2. **Shaft**: three blocks of dark stone stacked on the heart, and the configuration's practice carried through twice.\
3. **Crown**: the configuration's crown on the shaft, and the Kindling rite completed at a Lesser Circle within 12 blocks.\
4. **Kindling**: the spire's upkeep held three days in a row.

The Crown is finished by **the Kindling**, a ritual at a Lesser Circle within 12 blocks of the heart, taught by Circle Lore: Kindles a Concord Spire within 12 blocks whose crown stands: each participant is shielded for two minutes, and the spire's Crown is finished.\
\
**Offer:** 8 Glowstone Dust, 2 Gold Ingot, 1 Ender Pearl.\
**Takes:** one practitioner, 8 Focus each, 6 steps (12 seconds), drawing 2 Ley Charge from each pylon a step (48 in all).

**Needs:** First Light mastered and Circle Lore understood; its keepers complete rituals.\
**Crown:** lumen sconce over glowstone.\
**Upkeep a day:** 4 glowstone dust and 8 Ley Charge.\
**Its field** kindles light in the dark open air within 24 blocks, so nothing hostile spawns there, at most 4 at each pulse (every 5 seconds).

**Needs:** Verdant Husbandry mastered and Circle Lore understood; its keepers tend living devices.\
**Crown:** flowering azalea over moss block.\
**Upkeep a day:** 8 bone meal and 6 Ley Charge.\
**Its field** grows the crops within 16 blocks a step at a time, at most 6 at each pulse (every 5 seconds).

**Needs:** Celestial Attunement mastered and Circle Lore understood; its keepers observe the sky.\
**Crown:** lightning rod over amethyst block.\
**Upkeep a day:** 2 glow ink sacs and 8 Ley Charge.\
**Its field** restores Focus to its keepers within 24 blocks and reveals hostile creatures there, at most 6 at each pulse (every 5 seconds).

**/jugcraft concordance spire realign <configuration>** changes the configuration of the spire you keep nearest you, if you know what the new one needs. Before the Crown nothing is lost; after it, the Foundation and the Shaft stand, and the new crown, its Kindling and its days are done again.
Endgame works raised together and kept: the Concord Spire

From the Kindling on, each day the spire takes its configuration's item from the heart's store and Ley Charge from its own pylons. Put the item in by hand (use it on the heart), by hopper, or let a **courier** bring it: the heart files a request at a Courier Post within 16 blocks you may use whenever it holds less than two days' upkeep. A day without its upkeep takes nothing and the field rests until the next day that has it.

A spire answers keepers who keep practising: its configuration's practice carried through by its keeper (or, if shared, their party) at least once every 7 days. Unattended, it rests; the next practice wakes it.

The heart checks every part of the spire it has raised. If one is missing or wrong, the spire rests and says which and where; put it back and it works again at once. Nothing is lost: not its phase, not its days. The spire never breaks or replaces a block itself: its light goes only into open air and its growth only into crops. A Verdant Bed's crop it hastens grows by its own rules: its bed pays at least a nutrient a step, and a Mendvetch fixes none while hastened.

Use the heart with an empty hand, or **/jugcraft concordance spire**, for its phase and what it still needs, its upkeep and store, its field and its attendance. Jade, when installed, shows the same at a glance. **/jugcraft concordance spire abandon confirm** forgets the spire you keep nearest you; what you built stays.
Set up a Drone Tower in a few minutes, with endless power and building blocks. Everything here is in the creative inventory: search for it by name.
Lay a flat 15x15 square of chiseled stone bricks and place a Drone Tower Core in the very middle. A Drone Tower Foundation blueprint previews the finished tower (shift+scroll).
Take stacks of the Structural, Hangar, Armour and Avionics Modules and right-click the core with each, a few times over. It holds 1024 of each, enough for every tier.
Right-click the core and press UPGRADE DRONE TOWER. The core builds the command room, the landing pads and two exchanges round the field by itself.
Place it touching the Energy Exchange Port, the striped block on the west edge of the field. It gives endless power on every side, so the depot never runs low.
Place it anywhere within 48 blocks of the depot terminal, for example just off the edge of the field. Drones then get every building block they ask for, free.
Right-click the terminal with drones to link them. The Creative Drone is fast and needs no power. A tier N tower allows drones up to tier N.
Open the core and press UPGRADE again for each tier. Your drones fly every tier in until the spire is done at tier 9. For survival, craft the Field Manual (a book and a tier 1 drone).
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.1: A Drone Tower is a depot that grows. Its drones carry blocks and build for you, and every tier you add holds more drones and stronger ones. Turn the pages to set one up.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.10: Your drones build blueprints up to 250 chunks from the tower, wherever the site's chunks are loaded; the tower keeps itself loaded. You can build more towers, each over 250 chunks from your others.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.11: The terminal's mode (Personal or Party) decides who may use it. Place other blueprints and your drones build those too. The tower is lit, so mobs do not spawn on it.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.2: Print a Drone Tower Foundation blueprint at a Blueprint Table. Hold it and shift+scroll to see how big the finished tower gets: over 200 blocks tall on a 39x39 field. Leave room.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.3: Lay a flat 15x15 square of chiseled stone bricks. Craft a Drone Tower Core (aluminium plates, a processor, advanced circuits and a Drone Depot Terminal) and put it in the very middle.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.4: Tiers are built from Structural, Hangar, Armour and Avionics Modules. Right-click the core holding them, or feed them in with pipes or conveyors. Right-click the core to see what the next tier needs.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.5: Press UPGRADE DRONE TOWER. The core builds tier 1 itself: eight landing pads, the command room with the depot terminal, and two exchanges on the edges of the field.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.6: The Energy Exchange stands on the west edge. Run cables or put generators against its Energy Exchange Port (the striped block). That powers every drone; low power only slows them.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.7: The Storage Exchange stands on the east edge. Pipes, conveyors and hoppers against its Cargo Exchange Port fill the depot's store, and drones take the blocks for every job from there.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.8: Right-click the terminal or a landing pad with a drone to link it. A tier N tower allows drones up to tier N. Tier 1 holds 32 drones; a finished tower holds 133.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.9: Load the next tier's modules and press UPGRADE again. From tier 2 on, your drones fly each tier in, from the bottom up, as long as power and blocks keep coming.

component.jugcraft.allies.description: Acts on you and the members of your party nearest to where the spell lands. Only helpful operations may choose allies.
component.jugcraft.cinder.description: Cinderbolt's burning shard: fire damage that grows with fire Spell Power.
component.jugcraft.creatures.description: Acts on the creatures nearest to where the spell lands. A harmful operation never touches you.
component.jugcraft.extend.description: Eight blocks further: joined to touch or ray.
component.jugcraft.flare.description: Hearthflare's burst: fire damage that grows with fire Spell Power.
component.jugcraft.flash.description: Flashstep's push: forward, the way you face.
component.jugcraft.here.description: The spell lands where you stand; after then, where the spell before it landed.
component.jugcraft.intensify.description: Half as strong again (at least one more): joined to an operation.
component.jugcraft.kindle_light.descript: Kindle's mote: steady light for a minute.
component.jugcraft.kindling.description: Hearthspark's spark: kindles an unlit campfire, candle or candle cake.
component.jugcraft.lance_beam.descriptio: The Lance's beam: arcane damage that grows with arcane Spell Power.
component.jugcraft.light.description: Sets a Kindled mote in open air you may build in.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_accelerate.de: Increases the speed of projectile spells.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_amplify.descr: Additively increases the power of most spell effects. Can increase the harvest level of Break and increases the damage of spells.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_animate_block: Animates a block to fight for you. The animated block will convert to a falling block when it dies. Costs a large amount of mana, but does not grant Summoning Sickness
component.jugcraft.nouveau_aoe.descripti: Spells will affect a larger area around a targeted block.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_blink.descrip: Teleports the caster to a location. If an entity is hit and the caster is holding a Warp Scroll in the offhand, the entity will be warped to the location on the Warp Scroll. When used on Self, the caster blinks forward. Spell Turrets and Runes can warp entities using Warp Scrolls from adjacent inventories without consuming the scroll.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_bounce.descri: Gives players the Bounce effect, causing them to bounce upwards upon falling. Amplification of Bounce will preserve additional forward facing motion per bounce.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_break.descrip: Breaks blocks of an average hardness. Can be amplified to increase the harvest level. Sensitive will simulate breaking blocks with Shears instead of a pickaxe.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_bubble.descri: Captures mobs and entities it touches, causing them to float upwards. If the bubble has been alive for at least one tick, damaging the entity trapped in the bubble will cause it to pop, dealing bonus damage to the entity inside. Extend time and amplify can be used to increase the duration and damage of the bubble.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_burst.descrip: Resolves the spell in a spherical area around the target. Augment with Sensitive to target blocks instead of entities and Dampen to make an empty sphere. Augment with AOE to increase the radius.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_cold_snap.des: Causes wet, slowed, or freezing entities to take a burst of damage and erupt into falling ice. Falling ice will slow and damage nearby entities. Can also be used to erupt a block of ice instead. Falling blocks of ice can be manipulated with the Focus of Block Shaping. Entities afflicted with Freezing will be set to the maximum freeze level immediately.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_conjure_water: Places water at a location or extinguishes entities on fire. If augmented with extend time, it will keep entities wet for a longer period of time.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_crush.descrip: Turns stone into gravel, and gravel into sand. Will also crush flowers into bonus dye. Need Sensitive to work on items. For full recipe support, see JEI. Will also harm entities and deals bonus damage to entities that are swimming.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_cut.descripti: Simulates using shears on entities and blocks, or damages non-shearable entities for a small amount. Amplify will simulate using an Axe instead of Shears. For simulating breaking with shears, see Break and Sensitive. Costs nothing.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_dampen.descri: Decreases the power of most spells.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_decelerate.de: Decreases the speed of projectile spells.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_delay.descrip: Delays the resolution of effects placed to the right of this spell for a few moments. The delay may be increased with the Extend Time augment, or decreased with Duration Down.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_dispel.descri: Removes any potion effects on the target. When used on a witch at half health, the witch will vanish in return for a Wixie shard. Will also dispel tamed summons back into their charm.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_duration_down: Reduces the duration of spells like potion effects, delay, redstone signal, and others.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_ender_invento: Opens your personal ender chest inventory from anywhere.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_evaporate.des: Deletes fluids in an area. Can be expanded with AOE.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_exchange.desc: When used on blocks, exchanges the blocks in the players hotbar for the blocks hit as if they were mined with silk touch. Can be augmented with AOE, and Amplify is required for swapping blocks of higher hardness. When used on entities, the locations of the caster and the entity hit are swapped.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_explosion.des: Causes an explosion at the location. Amplify increases the damage and size by a small amount, while AOE will increase the size of the explosion by a large amount, but not damage.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_extend_time.d: Extends the time that spells last, including buffs, fangs, and summons
component.jugcraft.nouveau_extract.descr: Applies a silk-touch effect to Break and causes Explosion to not destroy blocks that drop. Cannot be combined with Fortune.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_fangs.descrip: Summons Evoker Fangs in the direction where the spell was targeted. Using fangs on your self will spawn them in an area around you.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_fell.descript: Harvests entire trees, mushrooms, cactus, and other vegetation. Can be amplified with Amplify to break materials of higher hardness. AOE will increase the number of blocks that may be broken at one time.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_firework.desc: Creates a firework at the location or entity. Amplify will add Firework Stars, while Extend Time will add additional flight time. If a firework exists in the casters inventory, the created firework will mimic the held one. Spell Turrets with Touch will create fireworks as if they were dispensed.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_flare.descrip: When used on an entity or block that is on fire or afflicted with Blasting, Cinders will explode around the target, dealing damage and creating Mage Fire nearby. Mage Fire cannot spread to blocks and is short lived. Entities with Blasting will immediately explode for extra strength.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_fortune.descr: Increases the drop chance from mobs killed by Damage and blocks that are destroyed by Break. Cannot be combined with Extract.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_freeze.descri: Freezes water or lava in a small area or slows a target for a short time. Freeze on Ice will turn it into Packed Ice, and Packed Ice into Blue Ice. Sensitive will turn water into Frosted Ice and will vanish after a short time.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_glide.descrip: Grants the Glide effect, allowing the wearer to fly as if they were wearing an Elytra.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_gravity.descr: Causes blocks and entities to fall. When augmented with Extend Time, players will have their flight disabled and will obtain the Gravity effect. While afflicted with Gravity, entities will rapidly fall and take double falling damage.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_grow.descript: Causes plants to accelerate in growth as if they were bonemealed.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_gust.descript: Knocks a target or block away a short distance from the caster. Sensitive will stop this spell from launching blocks.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_harm.descript: Damages a target. May be increased by Amplify, or applies the Poison debuff when using a Time augment. Note, multiple Harms without a delay will not apply due to invincibility on hit.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_harvest.descr: When used on grown crops, this spell will obtain the fully grown product without destroying the plant.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_heal.descript: Heals a small amount of health and consumes hunger from the caster. When used on Undead, the spell will deal an equal amount of magic damage.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_hex.descripti: Applies the Hex effect. Hex increases any damage taken by a small amount while the user is afflicted by poison, wither, fire, or when frozen. Additionally, Hex cuts the rate of Mana Regeneration and healing in half.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_ignite.descri: Sets blocks and mobs on fire for a short time. Sensitive will summon Mage Fire, a shorter lived fire that will not spread or destroy blocks.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_infuse.descri: Infuses a target with a potion or flask from your inventory. If augmented with AOE, a splash potion will spawn at the location. If augmented with Extend Time, a lingering potion will spawn at the location. Caster blocks may pull from adjacent Potion Jars to cast infuse.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_intangible.de: Causes blocks to temporarily turn into air. Can be modified with Amplify for blocks of higher hardness, AOE, Duration Down, and Extend Time.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_interact.desc: Interacts with blocks or entities as it were a player. Useful for reaching levers, chests, or animals. Sensitive will use your off-hand item on the block or entity, Amplify will use left-click instead of right-click on blocks.
Causes the target to turn invisible for a short time.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_launch.descri: Launches an entity or block into the air. Can be used for large jumps, yeeting mobs in the sky or for scaling mountains! Sensitive will stop this spell from launching blocks.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_leap.descript: Launches the target in the direction they are looking. Amplification will increase the distance moved.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_light.descrip: If cast on a block, a permanent light source is created. May be amplified up to Glowstone brightness, or Dampened for a lower light level. When cast on yourself, you will receive night vision. When cast on other entities or with Sensitive, they will receive Night Vision and Glowing. If Sensitive, Glowing will use the spell color. Particles can be configured from the Spell Style menu in the spellbook.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_lightning.des: Summons a lightning bolt at the location. Entities struck will be given the Shocked effect. Shocked causes all additional lightning damage to deal bonus damage, and increases the level of Shocked up to III. Lightning also deals bonus damage to entities that are wet or wearing RF powered items. Can be augmented with Amplify, Dampen, and Extend Time.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_linger.descri: Creates a lingering field that applies spells on nearby entities for a short time. Applying Sensitive will make this spell target blocks instead. AOE will expand the effective range, Accelerate will cast spells faster, Dampen will ignore gravity, and Extend Time will increase the duration.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_name.descript: Names an entity after the set Spell Name. Targeting a block will name nearby entities or name inventory blocks directly if possible. Targeting with Self will name the held offhand item. Can be overridden with a name tag in the hotbar.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_orbit.descrip: Summons three orbiting projectiles around the target that will cast a spell on any entities it may hit. Additional projectiles, their speed, radius, and duration may be augmented. Sensitive will cause Orbit to hit blocks.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_pantomime.des: Applies spells to the nearest block in your line of sight. Dampen will reduce the distance, Amplify will increase it. Sensitive will highlight the selected block.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_phantom_block: Creates a temporary block that will disappear after a short time. Amplify will cause the block to be permanent. Dispelling this block will destroy it instantly. Casting on an entity will create blocks around them in the upwards direction.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_pickup.descri: Picks up nearby items in a medium radius where this spell is activated. The range may be expanded with AOE.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_pierce.descri: When applied to the Projectile spell, projectiles may continue through their path an additional time after hitting a mob or block. Causes certain effects to also target the block behind them, like Break. Combines with AOE to provide depth.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_place_block.d: Places blocks from the casters inventory. If cast by a player, this spell will place blocks from the hot bar first. Casting on an entity will place the blocks beneath the entity in the up direction. Sensitive causes the block to be placed in the caster's facing direction, two Sensitives will place it in the opposite direction.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_prestidigitat: Places an invisible temporary block that emits particles. Amplify will make this block permanent. Particles can be configured from the Spell Style menu in the spellbook. Targeting an entity will emit particles centered on them instead.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_projectile.de: Summons a projectile that applies spell effects when this projectile hits a target or block. Sensitive will allow Projectiles to break plants or other materials that do not block motion.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_pull.descript: Pulls the target closer to the caster. When used on blocks, they become falling blocks with motion towards the side of the block that was hit. Sensitive will stop this spell from pulling blocks.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_randomize.des: Randomize the behavior of some glyphs. If used with spells like Place Block and Exchange, it will randomize the block that is placed between the blocks in your hotbar.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_redstone_sign: Places a temporary block of redstone with configurable power and duration. Augment with Sensitive to set the target block as a power source for itself and surrounding blocks. Dampen and Amplify will adjust the power from the base value of 10.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_reset.descrip: Resets the spell chain to the original target if it was changed by a previous effect. For example, Burst -> Place Block -> Reset -> Break will cause Burst to place blocks, but only Break will apply to the original location. As a result, using Reset will allow you to bypass combination and duplicate limits on glyphs.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_rewind.descri: Rewinds an entity back in time to its previous locations and health. Can revert blocks that were moved with spells back into solid blocks. Glyphs that come after Rewind will be cast at the end of the rewind, as if they were Delayed.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_rotate.descri: Rotates a block or an entity clockwise. If augmented with sensitive it will change the axis of the block (if possible) or force the entity to turn their look. Dampen will rotate counter-clockwise.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_rune.descript: Places a rune on the ground that will cast the spell on targets that touch the rune. Unlike runes placed by Runic Chalk, these runes are temporary and cannot be recharged. When using Item Pickup, items are deposited into adjacent inventories. Sensitive will cause the rune to use the Owner's inventory for pickup and usage instead. Players with Magic Find will be able to read spells inscribed on runes.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_sense_magic.d: Applies Magic Find to the target, causing magical mobs to glow within 75 blocks of them. Magic Find also reveals spells on Runes.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_sensitive.des: Causes forms to target blocks they normally cannot target. Projectile and Orbit will target grass, and Touch will target fluids and air. Changes targeting rules of certain effects.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_smelt.descrip: Smelts blocks and items in the world. AOE will increase the number of items and radius of blocks that can be smelted at once, while Amplify will allow Smelt to work on blocks of higher hardness, Sensitive will make it only smelt items and not blocks. Dampen will cause Smelt to use smoking recipes.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_snare.descrip: Stops entities from moving and jumping. Extend Time will increase the duration of this effect. Snaring a block created from the Focus of Block Shaping will cause it to attempt to place itself immediately.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_split.descrip: Causes multiple projectiles to be cast at once. Each projectile applies a set of effects.
Summons a decoy of yourself. Upon summoning, the decoy will attract any nearby mobs to attack it.
Summons a saddled horse that will vanish after a few minutes. AOE will increase the amount summoned, while Extend Time will increase the duration of the summon. Applies Summoning Sickness to the caster, and cannot be cast while afflicted by this Sickness.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_summon_undead: Summons a number of Skeleton allies that will attack nearby hostile enemies. These Skeletons will last a short time until they begin to take damage, but time may be extended with the Extend Time augment.  Additionally, their summoned weapons are changed using augments, use Amplify to give it a better sword, or Pierce to give it a bow.  Adding Split after the effect will add to the number of summoned skeletons.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_summon_vex.de: Summons three Vex allies that will attack nearby hostile enemies. These Vex will last a short time until they begin to take damage, but time may be extended with the Extend Time augment.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_summon_wolves: Summons two wolves that will fight with you. Extend Time will increase the amount of time on the summons. Applies Summoning Sickness to the caster, preventing other summoning magic.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_toss.descript: Causes the caster to place an item from their inventory to a location. If this glyph is used on an inventory, the item will attempt to be inserted into it. Toss throws 64 items by default. Dampen will halve the amount each time. Amplify will double the amount each time. Randomize will select a random stack.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_touch.descrip: Applies spells at the block or entity that is targeted.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_underfoot.des: Targets the spell on the block beneath the player.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_wall.descript: Creates a lingering wall that applies spells on nearby entities for a short time. Applying Sensitive will make this spell target blocks instead. AOE will expand the effective range, Accelerate will cast spells faster, Dampen will ignore gravity, and Extend Time will increase the duration.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_wind_burst.de: Activates a wind charge at the target location, knocking entities back. Sensitive will allow the caster to ignore the knockback.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_wind_shear.de: Deals damage to targets in the air, with an increasing amount based on how high the target is off the ground, up to 10 blocks. Targets on the ground take no damage.
component.jugcraft.nouveau_wololo.descri: Changes the color of an entity or compatible block to the color of the spell.
component.jugcraft.prolong.description: Twice as long: joined to an operation that lasts.
component.jugcraft.pulse.description: Acts three times, a second apart, where it first landed. Its operations cost Focus for each time.
component.jugcraft.ray.description: A straight line of light: the spell lands on the first creature or surface it meets.
component.jugcraft.reveal.description: Makes a creature glow, seen through walls. Revealing another player counts as harming them.
component.jugcraft.sear.description: Light that burns: arcane damage, credited to you.
component.jugcraft.smoulder.description: Leaves the creature burning for a few seconds (Smoulder).
component.jugcraft.spread.description: Acts on the blocks nearest to where the spell lands that the operation can work on (lights keep two blocks apart).
component.jugcraft.struck.description: Acts on the one thing the delivery reached: the creature, or else the block.
component.jugcraft.survey.description: Revelation's sweep: the creatures nearest to you.
component.jugcraft.touch.description: The spell lands on the first creature or surface within reach.
component.jugcraft.ward.description: A shell of light that absorbs harm (Absorption).
component.jugcraft.widen.description: Two blocks wider: joined to creatures or spread.

jei.jugcraft.acquire.adept_wand: Not crafted or traded. With the default data, the Adept's Attunement turns an Initiate's Wand into it, keeping what was inscribed and tuned on it. Work it at a Circle Anchor in a Lesser Circle (4 Ley Pylons and 8 Warding Stones round it) with Circle Lore understood: offer 1 Initiate's Wand, 4 Amethyst Shard, 2 Gold Ingot and 4 Glowstone Dust. It takes one practitioner, 6 Focus and 5 steps, drawing 2 Ley Charge from each pylon a step (40 in all).
jei.jugcraft.acquire.dirge_skull: Not crafted or traded. Vesperine, the Last Reaper, gives it in the Hollow Acre, which the Last Rites open at night. With the default data, each share of her reward has a 50% chance of it. A share goes to each player who earns it in the fight by a blow, healing, a ward or an objective.
jei.jugcraft.acquire.golden_thimble: Not crafted or traded. Madame Tatterlace gives it in the Spindle Loft, which a Cursed Spindle used on a Spinning Wheel opens at night. With the default data, each share of her reward has a 25% chance of it. A share goes to each player who earns it in the fight by a blow, healing, a ward or an objective.

message.jugcraft.styx.gift: Styxhexenhammer: Take a cutting. Bring back a garden.
message.jugcraft.styx.line.0: Styxhexenhammer: Stolas teaches the stars. The greenhouse teaches patience. I find I need more of the second.
message.jugcraft.styx.line.1: Styxhexenhammer: The orchids are thriving. Their names are proving more troublesome.
message.jugcraft.styx.line.2: Styxhexenhammer: These flowers are still a mystery. For now, let them grow.
message.jugcraft.styx.line.3: Styxhexenhammer: Rituals and pacts will come in time. Tonight, I study the stars.

message.jugcraft.town.map_full: Make one empty inventory slot and ask me again for a free map.
message.jugcraft.town.map_given: Here is your town map. North is up: 1 Church, 2 Bank, 3 Town Hall, 4 General Store. The market surrounds the square.
message.jugcraft.town.map_hint: Need directions? Crouch and use a guard for a free town map. The directory is south-west of the square.
message.jugcraft.town.protected: The town is protected: you can't change it here
message.jugcraft.town.welcome: Welcome to the town! Here are %s Jugs to start you off. Spend them at the market.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.banker: You hold %s Jugs. Use a Jug Teller to send Jugs to another player.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.aut: Pumpkins, hay and orange banners. Perfect.
I've carried more pumpkins this week than a farmer.
Autumn's easy: if it's orange, it goes up.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.dec: That tree took me all morning. Worth it.
Red and white awnings, like peppermint.
Presents under the tree are just wool. Shh.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.hal: Soul lanterns on every post. Spooky!
Black and orange stripes for the stalls. Mwahaha.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.har: The feast table's set, hay's stacked, pumpkins polished.
Brown and gold for the Harvest Feast.
Carrying a whole cake across the square is harder than it looks.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.spr: Out with the old, in with the tulips!
Pink and white for the stalls this spring. What do you think?
Every window box gets fresh flowers. Every single one.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.sum: Yellow banners for summer. Sunny, like me.
The flower bed in the square was my idea.
Lanterns stay, everything else goes bright.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.win: Snow blocks for the planters, spruce for the windows.
White and pale blue. Very wintry.
Dark comes early now. I'll be watching.
Seen a creeper skulking by the east gate. Not anymore.
The town's safe. You have my word.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.guard.decembe: A guard's December: lanterns, snow and no surprises.
Somebody keeps putting tinsel on my helmet.
The tree in the square is under my protection.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.guard.hallowe: Skeletons in costume are still skeletons. I check.
The decorations are fake. The zombies aren't.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.guard.harvest: Even guards get a slice of pie at the Feast.
Guarding the pie table is a serious duty.
All quiet at the gate. Just bees.
Keep your blade sheathed in town, traveller.
Long watch in the sun. Still, nothing gets past me.
Monsters don't like the lamps. Neither do I, in this heat.
Move along, the square's that way.
Frozen solid on the wall walk. Still standing.
Snow hides footprints. Not from me.
Stay inside the walls after dark.
Harvest time! The General Store is buying.
The council has approved more pumpkins.
Enjoy our town, and spend your Jugs.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.mayor.decembe: Season's greetings from the town council!
The great tree was approved unanimously.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.mayor.hallowe: The council regrets nothing about the decorations.
Trick or treat? The mayor has neither.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.mayor.harvest: Eat, drink and buy something at the stalls.
A bountiful year for the town.
Welcome to our town! Mind the flower boxes.
The town council approves of spring.
Our walls keep the town as it ever was.
A fine summer for trade. Visit the market!
The Jug Teller in the bank keeps your Jugs safe.
Our shops buy fair and sell fair. I insist.
The town stands firm, winter or no.
The snowman has been elected to the council.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.autumn: We give thanks for the harvest.
The days grow short; the candles burn longer.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.decemb: The longest nights bring the brightest lights.
Goodwill to all who pass the gates.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.hallow: Fear not the lanterns. They are only pumpkins.
Peace be with you, and with your costume.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.harves: Share what you have; that is the feast.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.spring: Spring brings new life. Welcome to the church.
The bells ring for every season.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.summer: The rose window shines brightest in summer.
Rest awhile in the cool of the nave.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.winter: Even in winter, the doors are open.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.aut: The leaves are turning gold outside the walls. Worth a walk.
Pumpkins in every window box! Autumn's my favourite.
Bring your harvest to the General Store; they pay fair Jugs.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.dec: Have you seen the great tree in the square? The baubles glow!
Red and green banners on every house. Merry December!
I've wrapped my presents in wool. Is that normal?
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.hal: Did you see the soul lanterns? Gives me the shivers.
I'm going as a pumpkin this year. Again.
The pile of jack o'lanterns in the square glows all night!
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.har: The Harvest Feast! The table in the square is groaning with food.

screen.jugcraft.alchemy_storage.controls: Sort also merges identical stacks; Stack preserves first-seen order. Pause disables artifacts in this container. To configure or re-enable an artifact, take it out and use it, then return it.
screen.jugcraft.alchemy_storage.manual.b: Craft, find or trade for a Stone or tablet. Use it immediately: no research or study is required. Dissolve one plain item to learn it permanently. Choose its icon to withdraw it for essence.

All default item types have values. Dissolve rounds down; withdrawal rounds up, with no surcharge. Use 1 / 16 / 64 / Max. Search and favorites are optional. Empty charged or filled items before dissolving; their contents are never copied.

Next craft a Klein Star, daylight collector and condenser. Charge feeds neighbors; Fuel upgrades coal for the difference in item values. Loaded factories work while you are away. Claims, pause and redstone still stop them.

Bags have 54 independent slots. Sort and Stack merge identical items. Pause disables stored artifacts. Repair Talisman repairs gear; Black Hole Band gathers matching drops. Open menus pause automation. No nesting.

Use Density Gem or sneak-use Void Ring. Set allowed inputs, input limit and wallet reserve, then Start. Empty filters do nothing. Density makes iron, gold or diamond, one per second. Last status explains waiting. Your hotbar is not feedstock.

Add a pedestal for farming or defense. Its panel shows the effect, range and last cost. Gem controls show toggles and cooldown; bind direct powers in Controls. The HUD shows wallet, stars and last payment. Aim the Eye/tools to preview area and cost.

tooltip.jugcraft.alchemy_manual: Read six short alchemical reference sections. No research or resources are granted.

tooltip.jugcraft.alpha_pelt: The Alpha Werewolf's silver-grey pelt: tans into four leather, or binds a Howling Totem as a werewolf's pelt does
